evals.prompt: /mcp-swarm-compare Compare my last two runs of the docs-server suite and show me what changed.
evals.expected_output: The assistant compares the two most recent docs-server reports with the CLI and the bundled dataset script, checks comparability, and visualises the result labelled with the server name and URL or command.
assertions: The assistant selects the two most recent botz-run-*.json reports from .botz/mcp-swarm/runs (or the configured runsDir)
The assistant runs `botz mcp-swarm compare --base <older> --head <newer>` and treats exit code 1 as regressions found, not a command failure
The assistant runs scripts/runs-dataset.mjs from the skill directory on the selected reports
The assistant reviews the comparability notes before stating any regression
In Cursor the assistant hands the dataset to /canvas; in other clients it writes the HTML page with --html
The chart or page title and the summary name the server by name and URL or command
Every regression reported includes its before and after values

evals.prompt: /mcp-swarm-compare Show the p95 trend across all runs in .botz/mcp-swarm/runs. Some were run at concurrency 2 and some at 8.
evals.expected_output: The assistant builds a series dataset over all runs, warns that differing concurrency makes latency differences not comparable, and does not call those differences regressions without that caveat.
assertions: The assistant passes the runs directory (or every report) to scripts/runs-dataset.mjs
The assistant reports that concurrency differs between runs and that latency differences are not directly comparable
The assistant flags tools with fewer than 30 samples as having unreliable p95
The assistant excludes or calls out silent-green runs
The assistant does not start new load runs to fill gaps without being asked

evals.prompt: /mcp-swarm-compare Compare the last two runs of the triage flow suite, which calls github, jira and slack.
evals.expected_output: The assistant builds the dataset, keeps tools keyed as <alias>/<tool>, charts per-server rows and whole-pass latency, and reports flow regressions with numbers.
assertions: Tools are labelled `<alias>/<tool>` so same-named tools on different servers stay separate
The canvas or HTML includes per-server rows from `serverRows` (calls, error rate, p50/p95/p99)
A whole-pass p95 rise above 20% is reported as a `flow` regression with before and after values
Each server is named by alias, name, and URL or command
Every swarm command uses `botz mcp-swarm`, never `botz-mcp-swarm`
